title: picocli-jsonspec command spec
description: The JSON format read and written by picocli.jsonspec.CommandSpecJson: describes a picocli CommandSpec (a command's options and positional parameters, plus any nested subcommands) without an annotated Java class. Compiling picocli.jsonspec.CommandSpecDsl's DSL produces a CommandSpec that serializes to exactly this shape. Note: this schema is intentionally a little stricter than CommandSpecJson.read() itself, to help editors/validators catch likely mistakes -- see the two 'Stricter than the reader' notes below.

$schema.description: Optional editor-validation hint (the conventional key many JSON tools add/read for autocomplete, e.g. pointing at this very schema's $id). Ignored by CommandSpecJson.read() and never emitted by CommandSpecJson.write().

name.description: The command's name. Optional at the document root (an unnamed root keeps picocli's own default); required on every entry inside "subcommands", since CommandSpecMerger and ordinary use both need it to address the subcommand.

namedCommand.description: Stricter than the reader: CommandSpecJson.read() does not actually reject an unnamed subcommand entry (it falls back to picocli's placeholder command name), but that is almost always a mistake.

names.description: One or more option names, e.g. ["-v", "--verbose"].

paramLabel.description: Defaults to "PARAM" (picocli's own default) if omitted.

type.description: See picocli.jsonspec.ArgTypes. Scalar types only, by design; array/Collection-typed options and positional parameters are not yet supported.

defaultValue.description: Applied as the default when the option/positional is not matched on the command line. Stricter than the reader: CommandSpecJson.read() actually accepts any JSON scalar here (numbers, booleans) and stringifies it, but a JSON string is the documented, forward-compatible contract. Note picocli itself reports an argument as not required (ArgSpec#required()) whenever it has a default value, regardless of the "required" field below.

arity.description: Parsed by picocli.CommandLine.Model.Range.valueOf(String): a single count, or a min..max range where max may be "*" for unbounded.
